title: OpenAI Releases First Public Risk Report on Internal AI Models
summary:
The company's latest disclosure to the California Office of Emergency Services identifies mitigation strategies for frontier models that are not available to the general population. This quarterly report assesses the hazards of internal deployment, a vector Boaz Barak described as less visible than public releases, to satisfy requirements of Senate Bill 53. The law mandates that large AI developers share assessments of major risks arising from in-house model usage with the government.

OpenAI is the first AI developer known to share this mandated government report with the public, according to analyst Thomas Woodside. While other labs are required to provide similar risk data to California authorities, they have generally kept those specific filings confidential.
